transcript: Last night I went to see Leo poached out on Broadway. I saw it in September, early in its run, and I honestly didn't really like it. But it's been so critically claimed that when I had the opportunity to see it again, I figured it was worth another viewing. And I'm glad I did, because I definitely enjoyed it more the second time. I think because I didn't have to spend as much mental energy tracking all the events and all the characters throughout, it allowed it to be much more emotionally impactful for me. With that said, I still think it's a little bit overhyped. I just found it uneven. Like some parts are really spectacularly written and directed and others not so much. One of the main themes of the play is considering what is lost in family's history as generations move on in the wake of traumatic events. And it really comes together in the last act, set in 1955. But to build up to this, inadequately provide historical context. Some of their earlier scenes and conversations just felt a little bit contrived and overly descriptive. Arguably, it does pay off, because that last act is really, really incredible. But still, it wouldn't be my pick for best play. The Tonys this year with that. Another playbill for my collection.
reasoning: Creator enjoyed it more on second viewing but still finds it overhyped and uneven, with contrived early scenes though a powerful final act. Not a clear recommendation.
